extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of technical education, prospective Woolwich Polytechnic students, and readers of Nature interested in academic notices
extracted.subtask_description: Notices and requirements for courses and prizes associated with technical education at the Woolwich Polytechnic (session 1907–8), including attendance rules, eligibility, and fee-admission policy. Includes announcement of two essay prizes from the Association of Technical Institutions and where to obtain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association of Technical Institutions essay prizes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Association of Technical Institutions offers two prizes, each of 25l., for the two best essays — one on "The Bearing of Technical Education on Industrial Progress" and the other on "The Bearing of Technical Education on Agriculture and on Industries of a Rural Character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particulars of the conditions may be obtained from Dr. Clay, Northern Polytechnic, Holloway, London. (No further scoring or eligibility details provided on this page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecture enrolment eligibility for Bayliss physiology course
rubrics_metrics.description: A course of eight lectures by Dr. W. M. Bayliss (F.R.S.) at University College (University of London) is "open to all students of the University of London; also to qualified medical men and to such other persons as are specially admitted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies three eligibility categories: University of London students, qualified medical men, and others by special admission; no further admission procedure detailed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to attend both lecture and laboratory courses (physical department)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the physical department all students are required to attend both the lecture and the laboratory course in each class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance at both components (lecture + laboratory) is mandatory for each class in the physical department; stated as an institutional requirement rather than optional advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent attendance requirement for electrical engineering students
rubrics_metrics.description: Students of electrical engineering must attend classes in electricity and magnetism concurrently if they have no knowledge of the principles of electrical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a prerequisite/co-requisite rule: students lacking prior principles must take specified foundational classes simultaneously with their electrical engineering course to ensure adequate preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governors' fee-waiver/admission policy for Woolwich Polytechnic
rubrics_metrics.description: The governors desire that no young man or woman shall be deprived of the advantages of instruction on the ground of inability to pay the fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principal is authorised to admit students free who desire to attend any of the classes and to work steadily but are unable to pay the necessary fees — admission on the basis of demonstrated steady work and financial need; procedural details to apply not provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme contents: syllabuses and examination requirements included
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme of day and evening classes contains the usual syllabuses of subjects studied at the polytechnic, and particulars of the examination requirements of London University, Board of Education, and other examining bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme includes syllabuses and exam requirement particulars intended as a guide to serious students; time-tables of courses are mentioned as useful guidance. No detailed exam criteria are reproduced on this page.
